tryit.text: Radha has some five-rupee coins. Seeta asks how much money she has. How can Radha work it out?
tryit.think: Picture your own piggy bank. If you had 3 five-rupee coins, how would you find the total?

tryit.text: A, B, C and D stand in a queue. A is not at an even position, D is just ahead of B, and B is not last. Who is last?
tryit.think: Start with the pair: D stands just ahead of B. Where can that pair fit in a queue of 4?

tryit.text: A container has 20 blue balls and 13 red balls. Each button removes some balls. Sam presses Red, Green, Blue, then Green. Which balls are left?
tryit.think: Do one press at a time. Write the blue and the red count after every press, then move to the next button.

tryit.text: Johnny can carry 20 kg in all and already has a bag. How can he find the extra weight he can carry?
tryit.think: Say it simply: “20 kg is the bag plus the extra.”

tryit.text: Which option shows the correct number of minutes in (1/4 + 1/2) hour?
tryit.think: I know 1 hour is 60 minutes. Half an hour is 30 minutes and a quarter of an hour is 15.

tryit.text: Mani tries many times but cannot share his sweets equally with Swami. What could be the reason?
tryit.think: Ask why sharing works: 6 sweets split as 3 and 3, but 7 sweets do not. What kind of number always splits?

tryit.text: Rheya weighs 18 kg less than her father. Her father weighs 10 kg more than her mother. Her mother weighs 65 kg. What is Rheya's weight?
tryit.think: Write it as number sentences: Father = 65 + 10, and Rheya = Father − 18. Now it is just sums!

backcover_intro: In Class 4, children build on their first Computational Thinking skills: picturing shapes from every side, spotting patterns and breaking a problem into small steps. These are not just computer skills. They are thinking skills for every subject.
